bullets.title: US-Iran military escalation sharply widens, Strait of Hormuz contested
bullets.body: The US conducted its third round of strikes on Iran within a week, targeting 300+ Iranian military sites including missile/air defense systems, small boats, and facilities near the Strait of Hormuz. Iran retaliated with missile and drone strikes against US bases in Bahrain, Kuwait, and Jordan, and declared the strait 'closed until further notice,' though CENTCOM stated commercial traffic (140+ ships in the past week) continued flowing. Iran and Oman began talks on a potential median-lane mechanism to manage passage. Oil surged 3-4% at Sunday open; S&P futures opened down ~30bps; broader risk-off bled into Monday premarket with some recovery.

bullets.title: SK Hynix Nasdaq debut surges 13-15%, then reverses sharply; memory names hit globally
bullets.body: SK Hynix raised $26.5B in the largest US equity offering by a foreign company, closed Friday up 13% on debut, then fell 10-16% in Korean and US premarket Monday as investors sold the news. Samsung fell 9-11%, triggering a KOSPI circuit breaker (down 8-9%, worst in years). US-listed memory names WDC -5%, MU -4.4%, SNDK -5.3%, STX -4.2% followed. SK Hynix CEO warned that 2027 will be the worst supply year in memory history, with demand outpacing supply beyond 2030.

bullets.title: TSMC Q2 revenue hits record +36% YoY; capex likely raised to $60B+
bullets.body: TSMC reported record Q2 revenue of NT$1.27T (+36% YoY, at guidance high end); June sales were +67.9% YoY and +6.2% MoM to an all-time high. Management is expected to raise 2026 USD sales guidance to >35% growth and capex to ~$60B (vs prior $52-56B guidance), with 2nm and 3nm fabs targeting 350-400K wafers/month. TSMC is also building three additional advanced packaging plants, and its 1.4nm fab is ahead of schedule with mass production targeted mid-2028.

bullets.title: META +19% in July on AI monetization inflection; capex raised to $225B-$250B for 2027
bullets.body: META rose 11% in two days and +19% in July after unveiling a credible AI monetization plan via its Neocloud and LLM API (priced ~25% below competitors), and entering the frontier model race with Muse Spark 1.1. The Louisiana data center was expanded to 5GW/$50B+. MS upgraded META to OW at $775 PT; hyperscaler capex estimates from multiple banks now peg META at $225B/$250B for 2027/2028, up 29-22% from prior. JPM maintained Neutral, citing need for more external AI adoption evidence.

bullets.title: Hyperscaler capex heads to $1.2-1.4T by 2028; credit markets push back on issuance pace
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley estimates five hyperscalers will deploy $1.2-1.4T of capex by 2027-28, driving ~4x compute capacity expansion to 120 GW. Goldman and others warn the IG bond market is being stress-tested: $241B in AI-linked issuance YTD with Goldman noting capacity for only ~$360B more may be exhausted. Banks built record $4B net short corporate bond position. The capex arms race—META $225B, AMZN $308B, GOOGL $325-350B in 2027—is stretching credit, but equity investors still see durable revenue upside.

bullets.title: 2Q26 earnings season: 23-29% EPS growth expected; AI contributing ~60% of S&P gains
bullets.body: S&P 500 Q2 EPS growth is estimated at 23.6% with upside to 29%+ on historical beat patterns. AI infrastructure stocks are projected to account for ~60% of total S&P EPS growth and semis ~50%. Guidance trends are unusually strong: 44.4% of S&P 1500 companies raising guidance vs. only 13.6% lowering—near record. Small-cap revision rates are running above mid and large cap, an unusual pattern. Major banks (JPM, BAC, GS, C, WFC) report Tuesday; NFLX and STX report Thursday.

bullets.title: Fed meeting Jul 28-29 in focus; market pricing ~40bp of tightening; Warsh testimony ahead
bullets.body: Fed Chair Warsh delivers his semiannual monetary policy testimony this week alongside CPI (Tuesday), PPI (Wednesday), and retail sales (Thursday). JPM's Feroli forecasts headline CPI -0.20% MoM, core +0.22% MoM. 22V Research flags asymmetric downside if core PCE prints 0.25-0.3%+, which could trigger hikes. 2-year yields hit 4.23% (highest since Feb 2025); 30-year real rates hit 2.9% (highest since GFC). NY Fed's Williams set a threshold: core inflation at/below 0.2% monthly for policy to stay on hold.

bullets.title: Broad market technically constructive but geopolitical risk tests momentum at all-time highs
bullets.body: SPX closed at 7,573 Friday with VIX sub-15 (lowest since Jan 2026); SPY within 1% of ATH despite sector rotation. S&P futures opened ~30bps lower Sunday on Iran strikes before stabilizing near +0.35% by Monday premarket. KOSPI's 9% collapse (two standard deviations) is the headline Asia risk event. Hedgeye puts the immediate-term SPX risk range at 7,405-7,591; JPM year-end target is 7,800. Mag7 at ~1.17x P/E vs S&P (cheapest since 2016, vs 10-yr avg 1.53x).

bullets.title: Oil +3-4% at Sunday open on Hormuz closure fears; diesel/refined products the bigger risk
bullets.body: WTI surged 3.4% to $73.84 and Brent rose 3.6% to $78.73 at Sunday's Asia open on the US-Iran exchange. Jefferies' geopolitical desk notes that the principal inflation risk is now refined products (diesel, freight) rather than crude, as Russian refinery outages and diesel export bans add a separate supply shock. ADNOC set August Murban at $80.01. Goldman CPI model suggests fading oil/gasoline inflation near-term, with core PCE remaining in the 20-23bp monthly range.

bullets.title: AI breadth widening: 40% of adopters cite quantifiable impact; median S&P firm at double-digit EPS growth
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's 2Q earnings preview shows median S&P 1500 company delivering double-digit EPS growth—strongest since post-COVID recovery. 40% of AI-adopting companies cited at least one quantifiable AI impact in 2Q26, up from 21% in 2Q25. Ramp data across 21,559 US firms shows companies adopting AI grow headcount ~10% over two years, with entry-level jobs +12%, countering replacement fears. 22V Research flags 44.4% of S&P 1500 companies raising guidance, vs 13.6% lowering.

bullets.title: Memory shortage structural: SK Hynix CEO flags 2027 worst supply year, demand persists to 2030+
bullets.body: SK Hynix CEO stated 2027 will be the worst year in memory supply history, with demand outpacing supply well into the next decade. Samsung is accelerating its Yongin fab to 2029 (two years early), and Micron is raising its US investment plan to $250B through 2035. Samsung is seeking 20%+ QoQ DRAM ASP increases. Jefferies raised its 5-year cumulative China AI capex estimate 23% to $1T, with power demand up 31% to 34GW.

bullets.title: SHOP upgraded to Buy by Jefferies; software sector mixed—AI/cyber resilient, apps under pressure
bullets.body: Jefferies upgraded SHOP to Buy (first Buy since Jan 2023), citing strong 3P data, partner program tailwinds, and potential 2027 price increases adding ~3-4% revenue. UBS procurement survey shows AI/cybersecurity spending most resilient in enterprise IT, while CRM faces elevated renewal scrutiny and shelfware risk, and SaaS apps face license rationalization. MSFT and NOW seen as best positioned to monetize seat-plus-usage AI pricing.

bullets.title: GOOGL Cloud underappreciated: buyside expects 80s% growth in 2027 vs Street at 52%
bullets.body: JPM Tech Sketch notes GOOGL Cloud backlog is expected to cross $500B (ended last quarter at $462B), with investor 2027 Cloud growth expectations in the 80s% range vs. Street at 52%. However, Gemini is losing ground to OpenAI, Anthropic, and META in LLM rankings, creating a near-term product risk. GOOGL is also compute-constrained, having rented capacity from SPCX. MS models 77-78% Google Cloud growth in 2H26 and raises 2027 capex estimate to $325-350B.

bullets.title: Power demand super-cycle: Goldman raises US CAGR to 3.5%; PJM hits all-time load record
bullets.body: Goldman raised its US power demand CAGR to 3.5% (from 3.2%) through 2030, projecting 108 GW/947 TWh of data center demand by 2030 (23% CAGR). PJM set a new all-time peak load record of 168,158 MW. MISO is projected to surpass ERCOT as the second-largest data center market by 2030. MasTec acquired Superior Group for $1.65B to access inside-the-fence data center electrical work; ERCOT Batch Zero classification expected by end of July.

bullets.title: INTC: US admin support key to resurgence; 18A delays flagged but PT raised by Citi/UBS
bullets.body: Trump administration's support was described as critical to Intel's turnaround. UBS raised INTC PT from $83 to $121 and expects a beat-and-raise on strong DCAI/server CPU demand and Panther Lake (18A) ramp; Citi cut its CTSH PT to $45 on weak discretionary IT demand and deflationary AI pressure, while raising INTC PT to $365. Apple reportedly committed to manufacturing Mac and iPhone chips at Intel fabs in exchange for semiconductor tariff exemptions.

bullets.title: Broad market rotation signals: sector leadership shifting to Financials, Industrials, Healthcare
bullets.body: Multiple strategists (Piper, JPM, Roth) note rotation away from the crowded AI/momentum trade toward Financials, Industrials, and Healthcare. Hedge funds net bought US equities for the first time in 4 weeks, driven by short covers in Info Tech. Tech sector was most net bought subsector this week even as momentum factor had its worst 5-day period since COVID. CAT, TT, and AAON are top picks into industrials/HVAC earnings. Technicals favor buying semi weakness (AVGO, NVDA, CRDO).

bullets.title: Consumer spending acceleration: +5.7% YoY in June with $20B tailwind into 2H26
bullets.body: JPM macro monitor shows total consumer spending at +5.7% YoY in June, a seventh consecutive month of sequential acceleration; 2Q26 total spending reached +5.5% (up from 1Q +4.6%). Discretionary spending hit +6.1% YoY. Upper-income spending was +7.1%. A $20B net wallet tailwind is projected into 2H26 driven by One Big Beautiful Bill/COLA. Blue-collar wages grew +4.9% YoY, outpacing white collar for the third consecutive month.

bullets.title: AAPL sues OpenAI for trade secret theft; deepening Apple-AI rivalry
bullets.body: Apple filed a civil lawsuit against OpenAI alleging former Apple hardware engineers—including Tang Tan (OpenAI's Chief Hardware Officer) and Chang Liu—stole confidential hardware and manufacturing trade secrets. Apple claims OpenAI hired 400+ Apple employees and that the company also queried suppliers about restricted processes. The lawsuit signals deepening competitive tension as OpenAI plans a consumer hardware device by February 2027.

bullets.title: China halts helium exports; chips supply risk emerges alongside US helium-semiconductor dependency
bullets.body: China halted helium exports amid US-Iran tensions that also threaten global chip supply, creating a second-order semiconductor supply risk. Separately, Jefferies raised its 5-year cumulative China AI capex forecast 23% to $1T as China approved 400K H200 chips (vs 200K US-licensed), and Huawei's Ascend 950 die size was cut by one-third, raising chips per wafer from 74 to 137.

bullets.title: NFLX engagement concerns weigh ahead of Thursday earnings; multiple PTs cut to $92-$107
bullets.body: NFLX is down 10 of its last 12 weeks with engagement weakening from lighter original content in 1H26. Multiple banks cut PTs (KeyBanc to $92, Oppenheimer to $100, OPCo to $100) but maintained Outperform/Overweight ratings. Proprietary survey data shows 5x more subscribers increased viewing vs. decreased, and Netflix's ~$6 CPM is far below the ~$15 peer average, implying $4B+ ad revenue upside if it reaches parity. TF1 live channel partnership hit 18-month targets in 3 weeks.
